text: {"options":[{"id":"A","name":"Dynamic PK Substudy Events with CDISC-Aligned Domain Forms","summary":"Add the seven PK subgroup intermediate visits as dynamic events triggered by PK substudy consent, create dedicated domain forms for each newly added assessment, and expand existing efficacy and safety forms with required subscores and assay details.","pros":["Matches the protocol schedule and flowchart 1:1 by dynamically triggering V2.1, V2.2, V2.3, V7.1, V7.2, V7.3, and V8.1 only when RAND.PKSUB is 'Yes'.","Keeps non-PK subgroup casebooks clean and prevents unnecessary blank visit folders or manual opt-out entry.","Separates newly added assessments (VS, EG, PE, LB, BM, ADA, PRG, CDIFF, UDS, SU, DIARY, CM) into standard domain-specific forms for clean SDTM mapping and targeted edit checks.","Captures individual Mayo subscores, modified endoscopy criteria, AESI indicators, and specific TB/virology assay items to directly support FDA secondary endpoints and eligibility rules."],"cons":["Increases the total number of events, forms, codelists, and dynamic rules to configure and validate.","Requires updating review plans and cross-visit edit checks across seven additional event folders."],"tradeoff":"This design gives sites a protocol-faithful schedule that automatically hides PK substudy visits for non-participants and keeps every clinical domain cleanly separated. In exchange, it requires building and validating more forms, dynamic event rules, and visit mappings up front.","recommended":true},{"id":"B","name":"Parent-Visit PK Collection with Consolidated Assessment Forms","summary":"Retain the existing 11-visit schedule by recording all post-dose PK timepoints on parent visits V2, V7, and V8, and group related new assessments into consolidated multi-purpose forms.","pros":["Avoids creating seven new intermediate visit folders and requires no event-level dynamic trigger rules.","Reduces total form count by bundling body weight into Vital Signs, merging clinical labs with exploratory biomarkers, and combining screening infection and drug tests.","Speeds up initial build configuration and keeps the existing event schedule unchanged."],"cons":["Forces sites to log Day 2, 6, 10, 72, 76, 80, and 90 PK blood draws under parent visits V2, V7, and V8, obscuring intermediate visit window tracking.","Bundled forms require item-level visibility rules at visits where only a subset of assessments (such as body weight only at V1.1, V4, V6, and V8) is required.","Complicates downstream data extraction and query management when multiple clinical domains share a single form."],"tradeoff":"This approach minimizes build complexity by avoiding new visit folders and reducing the total number of forms. However, it obscures visit-window tracking for intermediate PK draws and relies on conditional item visibility within shared forms.","recommended":false},{"id":"C","name":"Static Full Visit Schedule with Form-Level Opt-Out Flags","summary":"Add all seven PK intermediate visits as static scheduled events visible for every patient alongside dedicated domain forms, using the existing PK performed flag to opt out non-substudy patients.","pros":["Reflects every protocol visit and clinical domain explicitly in the casebook structure without relying on dynamic event activation rules.","Preserves clean, single-domain forms for all new safety, laboratory, diary, and efficacy assessments.","Eliminates the risk of intermediate PK visits failing to appear if randomisation data is entered late."],"cons":["Clutters the casebook for patients outside the Mainland China PK subgroup with seven unused visit folders.","Increases site data entry burden and monitoring noise by requiring staff to mark intermediate PK visits as not performed."],"tradeoff":"This option avoids dynamic event rules while preserving dedicated forms and explicit visit folders for every protocol timepoint. However, it clutters non-PK patient casebooks with seven unused visit folders that sites and monitors must manually bypass.","recommended":false}]}
